sections.h2: Who handles a property tax bill in Lawrence County?
sections.html:
Four offices in Louisa handle the tax year between them, and the PVA and the sheriff list the same Main Cross Street address. Each covers its own step.

  • Property Valuation Administrator (PVA): 122 Main Cross Street, Louisa, KY 41230. The PVA sets the assessed value and takes homestead applications.
  • Sheriff: 122 Main Cross Street, Louisa. Phone (606) 638-4368. The sheriff takes payment.
  • County Clerk: runs the appeals board paperwork and, after April, the sale of unpaid bills. The clerk's site posts the current delinquent list.
  • County Attorney: mails the warning letters to owners whose bills have moved to the clerk.

Taxing districts set different rates, so the sheriff's bill and the PVA's assessment for your own parcel are the figures that count.

sections.h2: What should a Lawrence County owner know about the place?
sections.html:
Lawrence County was formed in 1821 from parts of Floyd and Greenup counties and has had four courthouses over the years. Louisa is the lone city and holds the courthouse. In the east, a quarter-mile concrete T-bridge links Louisa to Fort Gay, West Virginia, across the point where the Levisa Fork and the Tug River join to form the Big Sandy River. Yatesville Lake covers about 2,300 acres, opened in 1992 and is run by the Army Corps of Engineers for flood control and recreation. Alcohol sales are limited to Louisa city limits.

  • People: an estimated 15,765 in July 2025, compared with 16,293 counted in 2020 and 15,860 in 2010. About 416 square miles of land works out to 39 residents per square mile.
  • Housing: 7,737 units and 6,342 households, with 77.8 percent owned by their occupants.
  • Middle home value: $111,700. Typical owner costs are $1,216 a month for mortgaged homes and $386 for paid-off ones, while typical rent is $760.
  • Income: $46,772 for the median household, with 23.4 percent of people in poverty.
  • Work: 207 employer establishments with 2,950 jobs in 2023, a 5.9 percent rise over 2022, and a 30.1 minute average commute.
  • Broadband reaches 83.7 percent of households, and 81.7 percent of adults over 25 hold a diploma.

sections.h2: What is the payment deadline in Lawrence County, and what happens after it?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 sets the year-end deadline at December 31 and gives a 2 percent discount to anyone who clears the whole bill by November 1. January costs 5 percent extra, and February onward costs 10 percent. The state's sample for a $1,000 bill makes the late cost concrete: a $100 penalty plus a $110 sheriff add-on fee, so the bill is about 21 percent higher from February 1, before any commission.

Late-mailed bills fall under a state alternative schedule that allows 30 days per stage. Oil and gas bills also exist in Lawrence County. The clerk's delinquent tax page says its sale leaves out the 2023 oil and gas bills, so ask the sheriff whether one is attached to your parcel.

sections.h2: How does a Lawrence County owner fight a high valuation?
sections.html:
The sequence runs in order. Step one is a sit-down with the PVA's staff. Step two is the May viewing window for the roll. Step three is the written appeal, which the clerk must have by the next workday after viewing ends. Step four is a hearing before the local board about a month later. Only evidence counts at the hearing, so bring proof such as a description of the lot and buildings, insurance papers, construction costs and listings of nearby sales.

Written reasons follow any change the board makes. Hearings may be recorded, and a paid representative has to fit the categories in KRS 133.120. Skipping the board closes off the Kentucky Claims Commission.

sections.h2: Who can claim the Lawrence County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Eligible owners are those who have turned 65 and those classified as fully disabled. The 2025-26 deduction is $49,100, which means a $150,000 assessment is taxed as $100,900. Locally, 19.9 percent of people are past 65, and 17.5 percent of those younger report a disability.

The PVA's courthouse office takes the form. A claim built on disability has to be renewed each year. Two groups are excused from renewing: veterans whose disability is service-connected, and people Social Security or a state retirement system has ruled permanently and totally disabled.

sections.h2: How has Lawrence County's head count changed over time?
sections.html:
The count was 20,067 in 1910, fell to 10,726 by 1970, recovered to 14,121 in 1980, and since then has ranged from roughly 14,000 to 16,300. The 2020 census counted 16,293 residents. July 2025 is estimated at 15,765, about 3 percent below the 2020 base.

The same Census tables show 6,342 households, 612 veterans, and a labor force participation rate of 46.7 percent. In 2022 retail sales reached about $209 million and health care receipts about $81 million. A seller who needs to confirm the exact bill, the exemption status or a possible lien will find that the offices above can answer in a single visit to Louisa.

sections.h2: How does the Lawrence County Clerk sell unpaid tax bills?
sections.html:
Anything the sheriff has not collected by April 15 becomes a certificate of delinquency at the clerk's office, with interest of 1 percent a month. Letters from the county attorney go out, and the clerk publishes the list before the sale date. At the sale a registered outside buyer can buy the lien, and from then on the owner pays that buyer. The Lawrence County Clerk's website lays out how its draft-style sale works, which also tells an owner how much the buyer may be paying.

Lawrence County Clerk delinquent tax sale rules (lawrencekyclerk.com, delinquent taxes page)
ItemRule
RegistrationAt least 10 business days before the sale
Deposit$10 per bill, capped at $250, not refundable
Prior year certificatesSeparate list due 10 business days before the sale
Bidders per entityOne potential purchaser
Order of purchaseRandom drawing, lowest number picks first, in rounds
PaymentCash, certified check, money order or company check
RefundsNone after the sale

The lien on the land from delinquent taxes lasts eleven years under KRS 134.015, no matter who owns the property.

sections.h2: What should a Lawrence County seller handle before listing?
sections.html:
• Ask the sheriff at (606) 638-4368 for the current bill and any earlier unpaid year.
  • Look through the clerk's delinquent list for any certificate tied to the parcel.
  • If you have the homestead exemption, find out from the PVA what becomes of it after a sale.
  • Compare your assessment with the sales of similar houses before the May inspection window opens, in case a dispute is worth filing.
  • Agree on the split of the current bill in the sales contract.
  • Because the PVA and the sheriff list the same Main Cross Street address, one trip to Louisa can settle both the assessment question and the bill itself.
  • Ask whether any oil and gas bill is attached to the parcel, since the clerk's sale notice mentions them by name.

Owners who want no repairs or showings can request a direct offer. Any tax still due is paid from the sale money at closing regardless of buyer.

faqs.q: Where is the Lawrence County tax bill paid?
faqs.a: The Lawrence County Sheriff collects it at 122 Main Cross Street in Louisa. Call (606) 638-4368 to confirm the amount and the payment methods before you go.

faqs.q: How much does paying early save in Lawrence County?
faqs.a: Two percent comes off a bill paid in full by November 1, and the full printed amount is owed from November 2 to December 31 under KRS 134.015.

faqs.q: What comes first when disputing a value here?
faqs.a: A conference at the PVA's office. Without it the board that reviews assessments will not take the appeal.

faqs.q: How big is the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025-26. The owner has to be at least 65 or classified as fully disabled, and the form goes to the PVA.

faqs.q: Can an outside buyer purchase an unpaid bill here?
faqs.a: Yes, when the certificate stays unpaid until the clerk's sale. A registered purchaser can buy the lien, and the owner then settles with that purchaser.
